title: Console firehose scratch — Miguel
content:
Morning rapid notes — console + customer reports (raw, messy)

Context: customer reported intermittent missing traces in the hosted console (alerts panel shows 0 traces for short windows). Slack thread: #cust-ops -> pings from support. Reported around 03/08 15:20-15:45 PDT.

Immediate reproducible observations:
- Dashboard: Alerts -> Live traces panel shows empty spike at ~15:23; other panels show normal traffic.
- Query used in panel: sum(rate(trace_spans_total[1m])) by (service)  — when run in Explore returns data.
- Hypothesis A: panel uses panel-level time picker range + a custom transform that collapses buckets and accidentally returns null for that minute.
- Hypothesis B: short ingestion gap at the collector -> check logs and kafka lag around that window.

Quick commands I ran (keep these):
- kubectl -n obs logs deploy/collector -c collector --since=30m | grep -i error  # nothing obvious
- kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group trace-ingest-consumer — observed small spikes in lag at 15:22 but consumers recovered
- curl -s "https://console.redwood.ai/api/dash/panels/alerts/live?from=2026-03-08T15:20:00Z&to=2026-03-08T15:25:00Z" | jq '.rows | length'  # returns 0 in UI-backed endpoint

Notes from Lena (DM): 'panel uses a reduce transform with drop_nulls=true by default' — need to confirm panel config.

Short-term mitigation ideas:
- Replace drop_nulls with fill(0) for that panel to avoid showing 0 traces (makes UI less confusing).
- Add a tiny annotation in Dashboard: "Known short-window ingestion blips may show 0s" — temporary.
- Run a re-query job that backfills that 5-minute window from raw storage (if raw retained) and surface to panel.

Action items (personal todo):
- [ ] Pull panel JSON for Alerts -> live traces and inspect transforms (location: dashboard id 4421).
- [ ] Open a quick PR to change transform behavior and add an annotation to the dashboard. (PR draft: platform/pull/2310)
- [ ] Correlate with infra events: check autoscaler and node restarts at 15:20-15:30.
- [ ] Contact support to update customer with ETA on fix (TBD) and ask for exact workspace + screenshot.
- [ ] Run small backfill if raw retention available — coordinate with infra to avoid re-ingest storm.

WIP debugging traces:
- Collector logs show repeated 429s from rate-limiter from a downstream proxy at 15:21-15:24 (10m window). Proxy config likely throttling bursts from canary jobs.
- If true, that explains brief ingestion gap but not why panel query returns 0 while Explore returns hits. Could be cached empty response in the dashboard backend.

Follow-ups for SRE/infra: (send separate ticket)
- Increase short-term burst capacity for trace-ingest-proxy during canary windows.
- Add metric: ingest-retry-count per collector pod so we can surface spikes.

Customer communication draft (short):
"Thanks for the report — we saw a brief ingestion gap in your workspace during 2026-03-08 15:20-15:25 PDT that caused the Live Traces panel to show zero results. We're investigating root cause and will patch the dashboard transform to avoid displaying misleading zeros while we fix the ingestion throttling. Expect update in ~2 business hours."

Random scratch ideas to test later:
- Force UI to bypass panel caching using ?nocache=1 param — see if hits appear.
- Recreate the panel locally against a snapshot of production timeseries to step through transform code.

Questions I still have (to resolve):
- Does the dashboard backend cache query results for 1m by default? who owns that component? (tagging @Jordan)
- Is raw span retention long enough to backfill 24h? need storage policy check.

Misc quick notes:
- Customer: Acme Logistics (CUST-2021). Might be on dedicated capacity plan -> their ingest path slightly different (dedicated -> dedicated-ingest-proxy). Confirm.
- PR 2310 is a stub; will not ship without review. Keep small change.

Short log of today's timeline: 
- 08:12 — PM ping re: customer email
- 09:03 — looked into dashboard queries, reproduced 0s
- 09:45 — ran kafka and collector quick checks
- 10:05 — flagged to Lena and Jordan, created INF-4783
- 11:30 — found 429s in collector logs, noted potential throttling
- 12:15 — draft customer message and this note (saving)

End of scratch for now — will tidy before moving to shared drive project doc.
